claims.text: External iliac → femoral: the external iliac artery leaves the body cavity and becomes the femoral artery, supplying the lower limb.
claims.quote: External iliac artery Branch of the common iliac artery that leaves the body cavity and becomes a femoral artery; supplies blood to the lower limbs
claims.locator: Table: Vessels of the Abdominal Aorta

claims.text: Deep femoral artery: a branch of the femoral artery that gives rise to the lateral circumflex arteries.
claims.quote: Deep femoral artery Branch of the femoral artery; gives rise to the lateral circumflex arteries
claims.locator: Table: Arteries Serving the Lower Limbs

claims.text: Popliteal artery: the femoral artery behind the knee; it branches into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.
claims.quote: As the femoral artery passes posterior to the knee near the popliteal fossa, it is called the popliteal artery. The popliteal artery branches into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.

claims.text: Dorsalis pedis: the anterior tibial artery runs between the tibia and fibula and becomes the dorsalis pedis artery at the tarsal region.
claims.quote: The anterior tibial artery is located between the tibia and fibula, and supplies blood to the muscles and integument of the anterior tibial region. Upon reaching the tarsal region, it becomes the dorsalis pedis artery, which branches repeatedly and provides blood to the tarsal and dorsal regions of the foot.

claims.text: Posterior tibial artery: supplies the posterior leg and gives off the fibular (peroneal) artery.
claims.quote: The posterior tibial artery provides blood to the muscles and integument on the posterior surface of the tibial region. The fibular or peroneal artery branches from the posterior tibial artery.

claims.text: Great saphenous vein: a superficial vein of the thigh with no arterial counterpart.
claims.quote: some superficial veins, such as the great saphenous vein in the femoral region, have no arterial counterpart.

claims.text: Venous return: blood from the abdomen, pelvis and lower limbs enters the inferior vena cava.
claims.quote: Beneath the diaphragm, systemic venous flow enters the inferior vena cava, that is, blood from the abdominal and pelvic regions and the lower limbs.
